messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SLO ALERT: p99 latency for /v2/stream > 12s over last 5m (streaming stalls reported). Auto-page to #incidents oncall.

alex: oncall here, looking. seeing spike on p99 and a lot of streaming stall traces (stall at "send_chunk" hooking into kv-cache). any recent deploys?

maria: no infra deploys in last hour. noticed higher GPU I/O wait on shared-gpu pool for cluster-g5. Some tenants showing sustained IO wait > 200ms.

devon: grabbing metrics and top tenants. running quick query: `SELECT tenant_id, p99_latency FROM telemetry.stream_latency WHERE window='5m' ORDER BY p99_latency DESC LIMIT 5;`

devon: results: t-1872 -> 18.1s, t-4410 -> 16.7s, t-999 -> 15.3s, others 7-9s.

jess: customer-ops says two customers reported streaming stalls and partial transcripts dropping. cc @customer-ops can you share impacted customers and SLA class?

customer-ops: customers A (enterprise, dedicated billing) and B (midmarket) reporting intermittent stalls. A is on reserved capacity fallback but some requests were routed to shared pool during autoscale.

alex: hmm looks like autoscaler routed burst to shared-gpu-pool because dedicated burst credit used up. shared pool is experiencing noisy neighbor IO. Can someone run `iostat -x 1 5` on the nodes under shared-gpu-pool?

maria: running now on node g5-shared-04:
```
Device            r/s     w/s   rsec/s  wsec/s  await  %util
nvme0n1          120.0   450.0  9600.0 36000.0  45.3  95.2
nvme1n1           10.0    20.0   800.0 1600.0   5.1   8.2
```

maria: nvme0n1 at 95% util, per-disk queue depth high. blkio cgroup shows tenant t-1872 using ~60% of write bandwidth.

devon: confirmed. pulled `kubectl top` on the tenant pods: t-1872 has 6 concurrent model workers with heavy writeback (model logging + checkpointing enabled?), and its pods are not scoped to storage QoS.

alex: immediate mitigation options: 1) throttle tenant IO via cgroup blkio limits, 2) move hot tenants off shared pool to a warm dedicated node, 3) enable model fallback (quantized smaller model) for the affected route to reduce write/kv pressure, 4) temporarily route streaming to region-dedicated as failover. Thoughts?

jess: prioritize customer impact: customer A is enterprise — prefer moving to dedicated or apply throttles carefully. customer B is midmarket — throttle + fallback ok.

oncall-janet: I can take the cgroup throttle and migration. alex, handoff in 10.

maria: creating quick blkio throttle for tenant t-1872 now. command:
```
echo '8:16 10485760' > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/kubepods.slice/pod_abcdef.slice/blkio.throttle.write_bps_device
```

maria: applied throttle, now monitoring iostat.

maria: iostat after throttle: nvme0n1 util -> 45%, write/s down ~65%. p99 for t-1872 dropped from 18s -> 9.4s in 60s.

devon: nice. still see a few streaming stalls for t-4410. looks like they have multiple short-lived large writes. plan to migrate t-4410 to warm-dedicated-2.

alex: creating migration job to drain t-4410 pods off shared pool: `kubectl drain --selector tenant=t-4410 ...` with graceful pod eviction.

jess: also flip routing to fallback quantized model for the stream route for tenants B and others with p99>10s. patch in route config:
```
route: /v2/stream
if p99>10s or tenant in [t-4410,t-999]: model_variant: gptq-7b-fp4
```

customer-ops: customer A confirmed partial recovery after throttle, will escalate to their SRE if we don't fully restore in 30m.

devon: adding monitoring checks: p95/p99 every 30s, streaming stalls count, nvme util. hooking into slack alert.

alex: summary of mitigations applied: 
- blkio write throttle applied to pod group for t-1872 (reduced NVMe util from 95% -> 45%)
- migration initiated for t-4410 -> warm-dedicated-2 (eviction in progress)
- route fallback enabled to quantized model for high-latency tenants
- autoscale config adjusted to prefer dedicated-burst when enterprise customers in route

oncall-janet: taking over primary oncall. alex handing off. key things for next shift: monitor p99 target, ensure t-1872 throttle doesn't cause application write failures, follow up with platform to add storage QoS for shared pool, and coordinate with capacity team to increase warm-dedicated pool.

oncall-janet: action items assigned to myself and devon:
- devon: complete migration and verify pod scheduling on dedicated nodes (ETA 15m)
- oncall-janet: run postmortem triage + customer-impact note and coordinate SLA credit if needed (ETA 1h)

jess: assigning follow-up to product/console: add automatic detection rule to detect high blkio util on shared pools and automatically apply soft throttles before paging.

customer-ops: customers A and B notified. A on enterprise support call, B sent incident update.

alex: thanks all. leaving notes in ops-runbook: `noisy-neighbor-storage` linking to this thread. :thumbsup:

oncall-janet: taking over now. will post a handoff summary in 30m and update last_message_ts when incident is closed.

-- Handoff summary (by oncall-janet):
- Root cause: noisy-tenant write-heavy workload saturating NVMe on shared GPU pool -> increased IO wait -> streaming stalls and p99 SLO breach.
- Short-term mitigations: blkio write throttles, migrations to warm-dedicated, model fallback for streaming.
- Customer impact: partial degradation for customers A (enterprise) & B (midmarket). Some dropped chunks in streaming, latency > SLO for p99.
- Next steps: permanent storage QoS, capacity increases for warm-dedicated, improve autoscaler routing logic, add preemptive soft-throttle detection rule.

oncall-janet: marking incident as active -> in-mitigation. will update when we verify p99 back under target and no streaming stalls for 20m. :white_check_mark:
